decision: The repository is created as a skeleton whose module contracts throw, rather than as a working slice of any epic.
rationale: The P0 design pack states that P0 implementation waits for BT-G0 and a Work Package with explicit, expiring authority. BT-G0 is unrecorded. A skeleton that tests its own boundaries is buildable without that authority; a contract with behaviour behind it is not. Every exported function therefore throws with a message naming the epic that would fill it.
alternatives: Implement the tenancy module far enough to be useful, and mark it provisional. Rejected: it would create the very claim AGENTS.md section 12 forbids.
Create only directories and READMEs with no code. Rejected: the boundary rules could then not be observed firing, so the repository would carry an untested instrument.
authority: operator instruction to build the repository from the guide, 2026-09-08

decision: The seven dependency rules are generated from modules/modules.yaml into .dependency-cruiser.cjs, and a hand edit of the generated file fails the build.
rationale: The P0.2 design makes the registry, not the checker, the source of the rules, so that swapping the checker is cheap and a module outside the registry cannot import or be imported. The generator has a --check mode that compares the generated files against what the registry would produce now; that comparison is the generation step of negative control 7.
alternatives: Hand-write the dependency-cruiser config. Rejected: the registry would then describe the modules while the config decided them, and the two would drift.
Use eslint-plugin-boundaries instead. Deferred: ADR-001 chooses the checker; the rules are generated, so the switch stays cheap.
authority: P0.2 design, dependency rule section

decision: The registry reader is a purpose-built strict parser for the registry shape, not a general YAML library.
rationale: It keeps scripts/ dependency-free, which is the pattern the P0.2 design names for the migration lint, and it lets the reader refuse a shape rather than silently accept one. A silent accept of a malformed registry would generate a rule set that protects nothing, which is the failure mode worth spending strictness on. It throws with a line number on any deviation.
alternatives: Add a YAML dependency. Rejected for now: the registry has one fixed shape and the reader must run before install in CI if that ordering is ever wanted.
Store the registry as JSON. Rejected: the file is read by humans deciding module boundaries, and it carries substantial commentary.
authority: P0.2 design, open question 5, the deterministic-script pattern

decision: Ten of the twelve negative controls of the P0.2 design are observed firing on deliberate fixtures; control 6 and every runtime control are recorded as declared non-coverage rather than passed.
rationale: Control 6 is a push straight to main and a merge with a failing check. Its refusal is the evidence, and only a repository administrator can create the protection that produces it, so an agent claiming it would be claiming a human decision. The runtime half of each control needs a running service and a database, and nothing runs. Recording them as non-coverage keeps the evidence honest; recording them as passed would make the whole matrix worthless.
alternatives: Omit the uncoverable controls from the records entirely. Rejected: a gap that reads as an omission rather than a decision is what the Architect stage rule forbids.
authority: AGENTS.md section 9, declared coverage and declared non-coverage

decision: The brokerage module named for the broker policy representation is registered as policy-record, not policy.
rationale: The migration lint refuses a P0 table named for the four domain words the security proof lists, one of which is policy, and ARCH-001 is emphatic that a broker policy representation is not the insurer-authoritative issued contract. The longer name keeps that distinction in the registry itself rather than only in prose, and keeps the module name from reading as the insurer record.
alternatives: Register it as policy and allow-list it in the lint. Rejected: an allow-list on the first row weakens the rule before it has ever fired.
authority: ARCH-001 section 9, data ownership; P0.SECURITY-PROOF control 6

decision: Mutation testing becomes a committed, required check, scripts/mutation-check.mjs, rather than a technique a reviewer applies once by hand.
rationale: An independent review loosened each rule in turn and found four that no fixture caught: rule 5 widened to any public file, rule 5 narrowed to internals, rule 6 narrowed to services, and rule 5b narrowed to modules. Each would have shipped a boundary that looked tested and was not. A one-time review finds today's gaps; a committed check keeps them found, and it fails on a lost anchor as well as a surviving mutation, because a mutation whose anchor no longer exists has silently stopped testing anything.
alternatives: Add the missing fixtures and stop there. Rejected: it fixes the four known gaps and leaves the next one to chance.
Adopt a general mutation-testing framework. Deferred: the rules live in two files with stable shapes, and a targeted list states in words what each mutation means.
authority: peer review of BIZTRUST-WP-001, finding F4

decision: The gates and authority blocks of current-state.json are enumerated in the schema, with each key pinned to the values legal today.
rationale: Both were declared as a bare object, so the two most governance-relevant blocks in the repository were unconstrained. A review erased every gate and forged three grants, including p0_implementation, and the validator returned exit 0. Pinning the enums means recording a gate or widening a grant is a reviewed change to a schema file, which is what an authority record should cost. It cannot be a one-word edit to a data file.
alternatives: Constrain only the key names and leave values free. Rejected: the forgery was in the values.
Add a cross-record rule in the validator instead. Rejected: the schema is where a reader looks to learn what a field may hold.
authority: peer review of BIZTRUST-WP-001, finding F3

decision: The migration lint normalises double-quoted identifiers, refuses an unqualified object name and a search_path change, matches domain words as stems, and walks nested directories. Its docstring now states its real limits.
rationale: The lint distinguished quoting style rather than intent. CREATE TABLE with quoted names matched nothing and passed; an English plural walked past the domain-word rule; an unqualified name matched no pattern at all despite a comment saying it was a failure; and a nested directory was never read. Four of the design's negative controls were defeated by ordinary, legal SQL. The docstring claimed the lint was conservative and would refuse what it could not read, which was the opposite of what it did, so that claim is replaced by the list of what it genuinely cannot see.
alternatives: Adopt a real SQL parser. Deferred: no research names one for this job, and P0.2 open question 5 assumes a deterministic script. The blind spots are now declared instead of implied.
Keep the text check and say nothing. Rejected: a docstring that overstates an instrument is worse than no docstring.
authority: peer review of BIZTRUST-WP-001, findings F1 and F2

decision: The generated configuration is stamped with the SHA-256 of the registry, and --check compares that stamp.
rationale: The header recorded the last commit touching modules/modules.yaml, which was empty before the first commit and never refreshed after, so it read uncommitted permanently. Worse, --check stripped the line before comparing, so the one field recording WHICH registry produced these rules was never checked. A content hash is stable across commits, is comparable, and is what the P0.2 owners table actually asks for.
alternatives: Refresh the commit SHA after committing. Rejected: a commit SHA changes when any other file in that commit changes, so it does not identify the registry.
authority: peer review of BIZTRUST-WP-001, finding F8

decision: A migration control asserts on the lint's MESSAGE, not only on the rule name.
rationale: Mutation testing found two controls that survived their own rule being disabled. A fixture carrying two violations of one rule proves neither: disabling the shape under test left the file still reported under the same rule name, so a name-only assertion stayed green. Each fixture now carries one violation shape and each control names the message it expects. This was a defect in the tests, not in the rules, and it is the same class of defect as an untested rule one level up.
alternatives: Keep one fixture per rule and accept the coarseness. Rejected: it is exactly the failure the suite exists to prevent.
authority: mutation check run under BIZTRUST-WP-001

decision: The secret scan reads bytes rather than decoded text, and the registry reader refuses an unknown top-level key.
rationale: The scan skipped anything that was not valid UTF-8, so it was blind to every binary in the tree; a review found a tracked bytecode file holding an assembled token literal the source deliberately avoids spelling. A secret does not stop being a secret because the file around it does not decode. Separately, the registry reader silently ignored unknown top-level keys, so generated_from sat in the file looking authoritative while nothing read it; an ignored field is a lie with a long half-life.
alternatives: Gitignore the bytecode and leave the scan as it was. Rejected: that removes today's instance and keeps the blind spot.
authority: peer review of BIZTRUST-WP-001, findings F10 and F12

decision: The migration lint denies by default: a statement that opens with a DDL verb and from which no target resolves is a violation, not a gap.
rationale: The lint modelled TABLE and SCHEMA and silently passed everything else, so DROP SCHEMA audit CASCADE, ALTER TABLE ... SET SCHEMA audit, and CREATE VIEW, POLICY, TRIGGER, SEQUENCE, TYPE, FUNCTION and MATERIALIZED VIEW against another module's schema all linted clean. The rule the lint exists to enforce is that a migration stays inside its own schema, and seven ordinary ways to leave it were unmodelled. An allow-list of verbs protects only against the statements someone thought of; the set of PostgreSQL DDL is larger than that list and grows. Denying by default inverts the failure mode: a new verb now fails loudly and is modelled deliberately, instead of passing quietly and being discovered by a reviewer.
alternatives: Add the seven missing verbs and keep the allow-list. Rejected: it closes the found gaps and leaves the eighth verb to the next reviewer, which is the same defect DEC-006 was written about one level up.
Adopt a real SQL parser. Deferred again, for the reason recorded in DEC-008: no research names one for this job, and P0.2 open question 5 assumes a deterministic script.
authority: peer review of BIZTRUST-WP-001, second round, finding NEW-2

decision: The four P0 forbidden domain words match as PREFIXES of an underscore-separated name part, deliberately, accepting that clientele and claimant are caught too.
rationale: F1 fixed policy(s)? to an anchored stem set; a second round found policyholder walking straight past the anchor, and asked for a decision rather than another patch. Prefix matching is that decision, and its breadth is the point rather than a side effect. P0 creates NO domain table at all, so the two error costs are not symmetric: a false positive costs one conversation and a rename, while a false negative means the phase boundary was crossed and no instrument said so. The rule is scoped to P0 and is to be RETIRED when the phase ends, not loosened while it runs.
alternatives: Enumerate every compound as it is found. Rejected: policyholder was found by a mutation, not by foresight, and the next compound would be found the same way or not at all.
Keep the anchored stems and accept the gap. Rejected: an instrument that a single English compound defeats is not an instrument.
authority: peer review of BIZTRUST-WP-001, second round; mutation M4

decision: badf/authority.yaml is itself parsed and validated, refuses an unknown top-level section, and must agree with the authority block of badf/current-state.json.
rationale: DEC-007 pinned the authority enum in the state file and left the registry the state file MIRRORS checked for nothing but a version line. A review appended a granted_extra: section carrying two forged grants and the validator returned exit 0, which is the same forgery DEC-007 was written to stop, entering through the door DEC-007 did not close. The two records could also disagree silently, the JSON pinned to NOT_GRANTED while the YAML claimed GRANTED, with no check reading both. The parser is small and strict for the same reason the registry reader is, DEC-003: it must refuse a shape rather than accept one it does not understand, because a section nothing validates is exactly where a forged grant lives.
alternatives: Add a YAML dependency to parse the file properly. Rejected for the reason in DEC-003, and because a general parser would accept the forged section as valid YAML; the strictness wanted here is about the SHAPE, not the syntax.
Check only that the two files agree. Rejected: two files can agree and both be forged, and the unknown-section hole would stay open.
authority: peer review of BIZTRUST-WP-001, second round, finding NEW-3

decision: The M5 not-tenant-owned exemption applies to the statement it precedes, not to the file that contains it.
rationale: The marker was read once per file and then used to delete every M5 error the file produced, so one legitimately platform-owned table at the top exempted every table below it. A migration could then create a genuinely tenant-owned table with no tenant_id column and lint clean, which is the exemption swallowing the rule. Resolving it per statement inside lintFile keeps the exemption available for the case it exists for and stops it travelling. This was found as a minor finding, and it is recorded because its blast radius was not minor: it is the same shape as a suppression that outlives what it suppressed.
alternatives: Require the marker on every exempt statement and drop file-level handling entirely. That is effectively what this is; the marker is now positional, which keeps the diff readable at the point of exemption.
Remove the exemption. Rejected: platform-owned rows in a module schema are a real case, and no exemption means the first one rewrites the rule under pressure.
authority: peer review of BIZTRUST-WP-001, second round, minor finding

decision: scrub() becomes a single left-to-right scanner, and what it cannot represent it refuses: a quoted identifier carrying anything outside [A-Za-z0-9_], a non-ASCII character in an unquoted one, and a dollar-quoted body.
rationale: It was four independent global String.replace passes, and peer review round three defeated the entire lint with one apostrophe. PostgreSQL allows any character except a double quote inside a quoted identifier, so tenancy."o'brien" left a lone apostrophe that the LITERAL pass, running first over the whole text, paired with the next one further down the file; everything between was blanked. A migration hid a cross-schema table, DROP SCHEMA audit CASCADE, a P0 domain table and a table with no tenant_id between two such names and the lint reported PASS with exit 0. Four protections failed open at once on legal SQL. Every ordering of independent passes has some version of that bug, because each pass reads text the others have not yet interpreted; a scanner that consumes one construct from the current position does not. The refusals ride along because the same scan is the only place that knows the matchers are ASCII while PostgreSQL is not: a Cyrillic o truncated `policy` to `p` and walked past the domain-word rule, and the lint read a different name than the database would create, which is the one thing it must never do quietly.
alternatives: Reorder the passes so identifiers are unquoted first. Rejected: it fixes this instance and leaves the class, which is the mistake round two made and round three found.

Blank a dollar-quoted body like any other literal. Rejected: the body then becomes invisible, and the accidental protection the old code had (the global DML scan still saw DELETE inside one) would be lost. Refusing it is both stricter and honest about the limit.
authority: peer review of BIZTRUST-WP-001, third round, finding 1

decision: A file this lint does not read is a violation, not a skip: a non-directory under the migrations root, a non-.sql file under a module directory, and the .sql extension matched case-insensitively.
rationale: A .sql file placed directly under db/migrations was never opened, and neither was a .SQL file anywhere. The output said "1 file(s), no violation" while the file carrying DROP SCHEMA audit CASCADE sat unread beside the one that was. Round one's F2 was the nested-directory form of exactly this and was fixed; the flat-layout and casing forms were left, undeclared. On Windows and macOS the filesystem does not distinguish 0001.sql from 0001.SQL at all, so the lint and the migration runner disagreed about which files exist. A skipped file is the same failure as a misread one and it is quieter, so the walk now reports what it will not read rather than passing over it.
alternatives: Declare the file-reading rules as non-coverage instead of enforcing them. Rejected: the set of files an instrument reads is not a limit to declare, it is the instrument's scope, and a scope nobody states can be changed by moving a file.
authority: peer review of BIZTRUST-WP-001, third round, findings 2 and 3

decision: The authority reader's default becomes an error, the statuses come from closed sets, expires_at is enforced, and the state-registry relation is total in both directions.
rationale: DEC-014 said the registry "refuses an unknown section", and the records repeated that as an instance of the round-two lesson, invert the default rather than extend the list. It was the opposite: an allow-list of five section names on top of a reader whose default was to skip the line. Round three walked through it five ways, each of them legal YAML: a flow-style mapping (invisible, because an entry had to have nothing after its colon), GRANTED_EXTRA in capitals (invisible, because the section pattern was ^[a-z0-9_]+:), a tab-indented block, a three-space one, and an entry with no status line at all, which counted as a recorded grant because membership was established by the key alone. Each forged p0_implementation, the grant this repository exists to withhold, with exit 0. Separately the relation to the state file was one-directional, so a grant ADDED to the registry agreed with nothing; and expires_at, which AGENTS.md section 5 makes the whole mechanism of implementation authority, was read by nothing, so back-dating it to 2020 passed.
alternatives: Adopt a YAML parser. Rejected for the reason in DEC-003, and because a parser would have accepted every one of those forgeries as valid YAML: the strictness wanted here is about the SHAPE the file is allowed to take, not its syntax.
Keep the sniffer and add the four missing patterns. Rejected explicitly. That is the move that produced this finding, one round earlier.
authority: peer review of BIZTRUST-WP-001, third round, findings 1, 2, 3, 7, 8 and 9

decision: badf/gates.yaml is validated and must agree with the state file, the two lifecycle statements the acceptance check stands on are pinned, and a Work Package may not enter ACCEPTED or CLOSED ahead of its acceptance grant.
rationale: Round one pinned the gates block of current-state.json in the schema and left gates.yaml, which AGENTS.md section 4 makes AUTHORITATIVE for gate results, checked for a version line. Setting every gate to PASSED passed; deleting the delivery_gates section passed; recording BT-G0 in the registry while the mirror still read UNRECORDED passed, which is the worst of the three because the authoritative copy was the unchecked one. Separately, badf/lifecycle.yaml records ENGINEERING_READY to ACCEPTED as requires_human with the role "verifier, who is not the implementer" and forbids any transition into ACCEPTED made by the implementing agent, and no code path read that file: setting the work package state to ACCEPTED, resume_decision to COMPLETE and the checkpoint to ACCEPTED returned exit 0. A rule an agent can edit is a rule an agent does not have, so the two statements the acceptance check depends on are pinned; the rest of that registry is declared non-coverage rather than silently trusted.
alternatives: Validate all five registries fully. Deferred, and recorded as non-coverage: skills.yaml and agents.yaml can still be rewritten by an agent, and pinning them properly needs the occupancy field agents.yaml does not have.
Make gates.yaml the only source and drop the mirror. Rejected: the mirror is where the schema enum lives, and the enum is what makes recording a gate cost a reviewed schema change.
authority: peer review of BIZTRUST-WP-001, third round, findings 4, 5 and 6

decision: A protection this repository NAMES must be witnessed by a fixture that asserts its own message, checked by scripts/coverage-gate.mjs and derived from the code rather than from a list kept beside it.
rationale: Three independent reviews found the same defect in three different instruments, and not once was the rule wrong: the suite was green while the rule did nothing. Round one found four dependency rules that could each be loosened with no fixture going red. Round two found two migration controls that survived their own rule being disabled. Round three found that three of the four audit verbs and two of the four domain words AGENTS.md section 5 names had no fixture at all, so three quarters of that sentence could be deleted with a green suite. The mutation check answers "does this rule have a test that fails when I break it" for the mutations someone listed; this asks the question one level up and without a list. Deriving the protections from AUDIT_FORBIDDEN, P0_FORBIDDEN_TABLE_STEMS and the generated rule shapes means adding a verb, a domain word or a module without a fixture fails the build, which is the only version of this that does not decay.
alternatives: Add the five missing fixtures and stop. Rejected: that is what round two did with four fixtures, and round three found the next five.

Require every generated rule instance rather than every rule SHAPE. Rejected: rules 1 and 2 are generated per module and the fixture workspace has its own registry, so demanding per-module instances would fail forever on a design decision that is already declared non-coverage.
authority: peer review of BIZTRUST-WP-001, third round, findings 4, 5, 6 and 7; and the pattern across all three rounds

decision: Three claims the records made about this repository's own defences are withdrawn as false rather than softened, and the residual forgery this fix does NOT close is declared.
rationale: known_divergence said the round-two response was to invert the default rather than extend the list, and named the authority parser as an instance. That was false, and it was written in the same paragraph that stated the lesson correctly. The checkpoint said 110 tracked files when the commit held 132, a number carried forward instead of counted. completed_scope claimed one violation shape per fixture while new2_unmodelled_verbs.sql carried ten, three of them asserted. Separately, and more important than any of the three: a forgery that edits authority.yaml, current-state.json and the checkpoint CONSISTENTLY still passes every check here, because nothing in this repository binds a record to a human identity. That is not a bug to fix in the validator; it is the boundary of what a validator can do, and the mechanism that actually addresses it is the branch protection recorded under NS-001, where a second person must approve the change.
alternatives: Correct the numbers and leave the reasoning claim. Rejected: the false claim was about whether a defence works, which is the class of claim this repository exists to get right.
Add a signature or attestation scheme. Out of scope and out of authority here; it is named as the shape of the answer, and the approval requirement on main is the part that exists today.
authority: AGENTS.md section 5; peer review of BIZTRUST-WP-001, third round

decision: A protection is witnessed PER STATEMENT TYPE, not per message shape. Each extractor, verb, stem, clause and rule arm carries its own fixture asserting its own message and its own mutation.
rationale: Four independent review rounds have each found the same defect in a different instrument, and never once was the rule wrong: the suite was green while a rule did nothing. Round one, four dependency rules loosenable with no fixture going red. Round two, two controls surviving their own rule being disabled. Round three, three of four audit verbs and two of four domain words named in AGENTS.md section 5 witnessed by nothing at all. Round four, six refusals in the record validator deletable with the suite green, and both arms of rules 5 and 5b unexercised on the apps side. Sharing one message across several extractors is what makes a dead extractor invisible: the message still appears, produced by a sibling, so the control stays green. The cost is real - this work added 74 violating migration fixtures and took mutations from 24 to 98 - and it buys the one property this repository has failed to hold four times.
alternatives: Witness each MESSAGE once. Rejected: that is the coverage this repository already had, and it is what let three audit verbs and two domain words be enforced by code and witnessed by nothing.

Rely on the mutation check alone. Rejected: it tests the mutations someone thought to list. scripts/coverage-gate.mjs asks the question one level up, deriving the list from the code so it cannot drift from the rules.
authority: peer review of BIZTRUST-WP-001, rounds three and four

decision: Any statement that can change schema resolution is refused whatever its spelling, and an INCIDENTAL target no longer makes a statement understood.
rationale: Deny-by-default was introduced in DEC-012 and had two holes, each found by a different review. First, PostgreSQL documents SET SCHEMA 'value' as an alias for SET search_path TO value; scrub() blanked the literal before any extractor ran, so the statement reduced to set schema '' - the SET SCHEMA scan found no identifier, the search_path check found no literal match, and SET sat on the harmless-verb exemption. A migration could set the session schema to audit and then create tables, defaults and index expressions with unqualified names that all bound into another module's schema, and the lint reported PASS with exit 0. The comment in the file claimed SET search_path was the one exception; it was not. The same act reached through set_config() wrapped in a resolving statement escaped for a third reason. Second, and worse in principle: the expression-call and cast-type scans push a target from anywhere in a statement, and understood was satisfied by ANY target, so an unmodelled statement carrying an own-schema call - COMMENT ON FUNCTION, GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION, SECURITY LABEL - stopped being refused. A later change had silently narrowed an earlier change's default, which is the interaction no per-task review can see.
alternatives: Enumerate the spellings that change schema resolution. Rejected on the same ground DEC-012 rejected it: three spellings were found by three separate reviews, and the fourth would be found by a fourth.
Read set_config's first argument and refuse only search_path. Rejected: scrub() has already blanked the literal, so a parameter this lint cannot identify is a refusal rather than a guess.
authority: peer review of BIZTRUST-WP-001, round four, findings C1 and I2

decision: No test suite writes a tracked file. The boundary suite works on a copy and the mutation check runs against a disposable git worktree, which aborts if the tree is dirty at start and fails the run if it is dirty at exit.
rationale: tests/boundaries/module-packages.test.mjs wrote the real modules/modules.yaml and scripts/mutation-check.mjs wrote mutated content into the tracked scripts/boundary-rules.mjs and scripts/migration-lint.mjs, each restoring in a finally. Two consequences, and the second is the serious one. An interrupted run left a LOOSENED RULE in a tracked source file. And because node --test parallelises across FILES, the registry writer raced the lint's own child process on ordinary single-user runs, producing MIGRATION_LINT FAIL registry has no version against correct code - observed three times while this work was executed, twice against changes that were green. A recorded PASS was therefore not reproducible by construction, which makes it not evidence. AGENTS.md section 9 requires evidence to be reproducible and bound to a revision; this is the mechanism that makes the gates block honest.
alternatives: Serialise the suite with --test-concurrency=1. Rejected: it hides the race rather than removing the tracked-file writes, and an interrupted run would still leave a loosened rule behind.
Copy only the files each suite mutates. Rejected: the mutation check must run the whole suite against the mutated source, so the copy has to be a working tree.
authority: peer review of BIZTRUST-WP-001, round three, declared non-coverage item 13

decision: The registry floors - which skills are FORBIDDEN_TO_AGENTS or BLOCKED, which seats no agent may occupy, which governance paths route to which seat - are pinned in scripts/validate_continuity.py, not derived from the registry being validated.
rationale: badf/skills.yaml and badf/agents.yaml were checked for a version line and nothing else, so an agent could set record-a-gate and grant-authority to AVAILABLE, or flip may_be_an_agent to true on all four human seats, with exit 0. The instruction given during this work was to DERIVE the forbidden set from the registry so it could not drift; the implementer enumerated it in validator source instead and was right to. Deriving the constraint from the file it constrains is circular: an agent edits badf/skills.yaml and the derived set follows it. Enumerating in source means widening a floor costs a reviewed change to a Python file, which is what DEC-007 already decided an authority record should cost. The relation is checked in both directions, so a skill the registry marks FORBIDDEN_TO_AGENTS but the validator does not pin is itself an error.
alternatives: Derive the pinned set from badf/skills.yaml at validation time. Rejected as circular, after being proposed and withdrawn during this work.

Pin only the two skills a review named. Rejected: a third skill of identical severity, deploy, was found unpinned immediately, which is the extend-the-list pattern this repository has been burned by twice.
authority: peer review of BIZTRUST-WP-001, rounds three and four

decision: A test seam must not be reachable from the ambient environment. scripts/coverage-gate.mjs takes --tests-dir as a command-line argument, and reads no environment variable.
rationale: The seam was introduced as COVERAGE_GATE_TEST_TESTS_DIR so the gate's own witnesses could point it at a fixture directory. A review then pointed it at two comment-only files and got COVERAGE_GATE PASS 16 named protections, every one witnessed by a control, exit 0 - while all four witnessing tests, which spawned the gate with the inherited environment, passed alongside it. One exported variable in a workflow file neutered the instrument built to detect unwitnessed protections AND everything that watches it, together. An argument cannot be inherited, so no parent process, shell or CI env block can redirect the gate; the witnesses additionally scrub the retired variable and assert both directions, that the poisoned directory fails through the flag and reaches nothing through the environment.
alternatives: Keep the variable and have the witnesses delete it from the child environment. Rejected as the whole fix: it protects the witnesses and leaves the production check redirectable.
Give the gate no seam and test it only against the real tree. Rejected: the gate would then have no negative control, which is the defect it exists to find.
authority: peer review of BIZTRUST-WP-001, round four re-review; introduced and closed within the same work

decision: Every mutation declares the control that must catch it, and a mutation caught by anything else fails the run. The overlap between mutations and controls is measured and printed in both directions.
rationale: scripts/mutation-check.mjs answered 'did the suite go red?', not 'did the control that is supposed to witness this rule go red?'. runSuite() returned only GREEN or RED, so a mutation disabling one extractor could be recorded caught because a control witnessing a different extractor failed. The first honest run under attribution found what that had been hiding: 36 of 98 mutations were killed by more than one control, 45 controls killed more than one mutation, and two mutations were caught by a control that could not have been their intended witness. The worst had been rewriting the wrong rule for FOUR review rounds - the mutation named for rule 5 anchored on a string that is a suffix of rule 2's more-indented identical line, and String.replace takes the first match, so rule 5's arm had no mutation at all while appearing to have one. An independent reviewer re-derived this: of all 98 anchors, exactly one was ambiguous, and it was that one. The gate now refuses an anchor that matches twice, a mutation with no declared witness, and a mutation caught by a control other than the one it declares.
alternatives: Keep the red/green sweep and rely on review to spot a misattributed mutation. Rejected: four rounds of review did not spot this one, and the count it produced read as stronger evidence than it was.

Gate on every mutation having an EXCLUSIVE killer. Rejected: a genuinely broad guard would then need a contrived fixture. The population is reported instead - 42 of 148 mutations are killed by no control alone - so the number is visible rather than enforced.
authority: peer review of BIZTRUST-WP-001, round five

decision: A signature no agent can produce is the primitive that binds a governance record to a human. badf/signing-policy.yaml declares the governed paths and the accepted identities; the check verifies commit signatures over those paths; and while no key is enrolled it reports SIGNING_CHECK NOT_ENFORCED and exits 0 rather than failing.
rationale: Every guard this repository added through four review rounds constrains what a record may SAY. None constrained who wrote it, so a forgery editing badf/authority.yaml, badf/current-state.json and the checkpoint consistently passed every check - verified deliberately, not assumed. No validator can close that, because the validator reads the same files the forger writes. Git commit signatures are the available primitive: the agent cannot produce one. The report-rather-than-fail choice rests on WHO CAN ACT on the failure. The repository has precedent both ways - declared non-coverage reports honestly, the dirty-tree guard fails outright - and the two divide on remediability: an agent reading a dirty-tree message can clean the tree, while an agent that could clear an unenrolled-key failure would have defeated the primitive. A gate no legitimate action can make green is one the next agent routes around. It becomes a hard gate with no code change the moment accepted_keys names an identity. What is not optional is that the unenforced state announces itself: SIGNING_CHECK PASS is structurally unreachable while accepted_keys is empty, and a control asserts that string is absent.
alternatives: Fail pnpm verify while unenforced. Rejected for the remediability reason above; a permanently red check trains everyone to ignore it.
Say nothing until a key is enrolled. Rejected outright: an unenforced control that prints nothing is indistinguishable from an enforced one, which is the defect class this branch exists to close.
authority: peer review of BIZTRUST-WP-001, round five; the residual declared in DEC-021

decision: The signing check reads the real history: every git invocation passes --no-replace-objects. Enrolling a key is gated on first closing the .git/info/grafts sibling vector, which that flag does NOT close.
rationale: Two ways exist to make git report a history that is not the real one, and both make the check resolve its enforcement point to HEAD and report a PASS having verified nothing. git replace --graft HEAD produces a repository git reports as NOT shallow, with one commit; the shallow guard added earlier answers false and the bypass walks around it. That one is closed. Writing HEAD's sha into .git/info/grafts does the same thing, needs only write access to .git/ - strictly less than the replace vector - and git 2.53 prints a deprecation hint and honours it anyway. --no-replace-objects does not disable the graft file. It is open, and it is recorded here rather than in a commit message because the moment it becomes dangerous is a moment the records can gate: while accepted_keys is NONE_ENROLLED the check returns from the empty-keys branch before any line that could read as a pass, so no false PASS is reachable today. It becomes reachable on the day a human enrols a key, and that human must close it first. core.useReplaceRefs and GIT_GRAFT_FILE close both vectors together.
alternatives: Refuse when git for-each-ref refs/replace is non-empty. Rejected as the primary fix: it guards a moment rather than a property of the reads, and it leaves the check unable to answer at all in a repository that uses replace refs legitimately.

Close the grafts vector in the same wave. Not taken: the process allows one fix wave after a final review and no second, and the vector is pre-existing rather than introduced. It is gated instead of hidden.
authority: peer review of BIZTRUST-WP-001, round five, final review and its scoped re-review

decision: The .git/info/grafts vector is closed by setting GIT_GRAFT_FILE to the null device on every git invocation the signing check makes. DEC-029's closing sentence is corrected: core.useReplaceRefs is INERT against grafts and closes nothing there.
rationale: DEC-029 recorded the vector as open and gated enrolling a key on closing it first. It is now closed, so that gate is discharged. The correction matters more than the closure. DEC-029 ended 'core.useReplaceRefs and GIT_GRAFT_FILE close both vectors together', which reads as though the two settings are symmetric contributors. They are not. Tested directly against git 2.53.0.windows.1 with a real graft file present: plain git log, git --no-replace-objects log, and git -c core.useReplaceRefs=false log ALL still report the grafted one-commit history. Only GIT_GRAFT_FILE pointed away from the real path restores the true history. core.useReplaceRefs governs refs/replace and is wholly orthogonal to the graft file. Both the implementer and an independent reviewer built the environment and reproduced this, which is how the imprecision was caught: the previous two rounds each found a written claim about this same file that was false because nobody had built one.
alternatives: Swap --no-replace-objects for -c core.useReplaceRefs=false. Rejected: they are equivalent for the vector they do address, the swap buys nothing, and the existing flag is already witnessed.

Refuse when a graft file exists rather than neutralising it. Rejected for the reason DEC-029 gave for the sibling vector: a guard on a moment is weaker than a property of every read, and it would leave the check unable to answer in a repository that uses grafts legitimately.
authority: peer review of BIZTRUST-WP-001, round five final review and its scoped re-review; DEC-029

decision: This repository keeps TWO decision surfaces with a stated boundary: docs/adr/ holds architecture decisions a human accepts, badf/decision-log.jsonl holds engineering and governance decisions an agent may append. docs/adr/README.md records why the first is empty.
rationale: docs/adr/ and docs/decisions/ existed as empty .gitkeep scaffolds beside a decision log carrying twenty-nine real entries, and nothing said which belonged where or why one was empty. An empty directory that reads as an oversight is what the Architect stage rule forbids, and this one is not an oversight: badf/authority.yaml withholds adr_acceptance, every ADR the P0.2 design depends on is DRAFT_REQUIRED, and BT-G0 is unrecorded. The boundary is the one the authority record already implies rather than a new invention: if it decides what the architecture IS, a human accepts it and it is an ADR; if it decides how this repository is BUILT or GOVERNED, it is a DEC- record and tool_authority already permits appending one. DEC-002 and ADR-001 concern the same seven dependency rules and land on opposite sides of that line, which is the clearest test of it.
alternatives: Collapse to one surface and delete docs/adr/. Rejected: badf/authority.yaml names ADR-001 to ADR-020 explicitly, so the surface is expected to exist and deleting it would contradict the authority record.
Leave both empty and unexplained. Rejected: that is the state that prompted this, and a reader could not tell an unfilled seat from a forgotten directory.
authority: AGENTS.md section 9, declared coverage and declared non-coverage; badf/authority.yaml adr_acceptance

decision: The seat-bootstrap circularity is recorded as an OPEN governance defect with a costed proposal at docs/decisions/PROPOSAL-bootstrap-seating.md, and no agent adopts it.
rationale: badf/agents.yaml routes changes to itself with verifier: repository-administrator, so filling the repository-administrator seat requires that seat to verify its own creation. The same unfilled seat owns badf/signing-policy.yaml and AGENTS.md, so enrolling the first signing key and amending the charter are blocked behind the same loop. Nothing in the repository recorded how the loop breaks. An agent must not resolve it: tool_authority.may_not forbids granting, extending or inferring authority, and a rule deciding who may SEAT an authority is a larger act than any single grant it is already forbidden to make - it would choose the mechanism by which every later authority here comes into being. So the defect is written down with four options costed and a recommendation, and stops there. The recommendation is a bootstrap rule adopted once by operator instruction, because that is the only combination that both breaks the loop now and closes it for the next vacancy; the precedent for the operator half is granted.repository_scaffold, which carries its own honest_status saying such a record is not the thing the design asks for.
alternatives: Adopt the bootstrap rule directly. Refused on authority grounds, not on merit.
Say nothing until a human notices. Rejected: the loop is not visible without reading the routing table closely, and the two next actions this repository records both walk into it.
authority: badf/authority.yaml tool_authority.may_not; badf/agents.yaml routing

decision: The review method learned across five rounds is written down at docs/operations/REVIEW-METHOD.md, and the vocabulary is fixed in a root CONTEXT.md that governs nothing.
rationale: AGENTS.md requires a verifier who is not the implementer with fresh context, and says nothing about how that verifier should work - so the most valuable thing five review rounds produced was living only in a chat log. Four rules earned their place by failing first: build the environment rather than reasoning from the diff (a reviewer disproved a docstring, a report and a CI comment simultaneously by running git clone --depth 1); treat an implementer's "impractical to test" as the finding (one true sentence about one path hid six unwitnessed refusals behind it); read the whole body at least once (a later task silently narrowed an earlier task's default, invisible to both tasks' own reviews); and ask every instrument the question it asks of everything else (this repository put its own defect class inside the detecting instrument four separate times). The glossary is separate and smaller: "control" was doing two jobs - a negative-control test here, a governance control in the flow-control vocabulary - and an agent had used both senses in one commit message. CONTEXT.md fixes that and states plainly that it has no authority, because a glossary that reads as a second charter is worse than none.
alternatives: Put the review method in AGENTS.md as a new section. Deferred, not rejected: AGENTS.md is owned by the repository-administrator seat, which DEC-032 records as unfillable until the bootstrap loop is broken. docs/** routes to peer-reviewer and is writable today, so the next review benefits now and the promotion becomes a one-paragraph amendment later.
Leave the lessons in the decision log. Rejected: a decision log records what was decided, and nobody reads one for instructions on how to work.
No glossary; define terms where used. Rejected: that is the state that let one word mean two things in the same commit message.
authority: AGENTS.md section 9; peer review of BIZTRUST-WP-001, rounds one through five
